title: Cold atoms in an optical lattice
lead: Atoms in an optical lattice reduce to the Bose-Hubbard model of hopping and on-site interaction; its superfluid and Mott insulator ground states, the quantum phase transition between them, and how a trap's wedding-cake density and the interference of released atoms reveal it.
notes: Figure 11.15 is computed from the mean-field state; the book's image reproduces published data and is not shown.

figures.original_caption: Experimental realizations of an optical lattice potential always include an additional harmonic confining potential. In a strongly-interacting system, Mott insulator phases with different filling factor $\nu$ occur in different portions of the lattice, with a small region of superfluid (non-integer $\nu$) phase between them.

Experimental observation of the superfluid to Mott insulator transition [taken from Nature 415, 39 without permission]. (a) Expansion images for different values of $t/U_0$, with the lattice potential ranging from $0E_r$ (a) to $20E_r$ (g). The superfluid phase is associated with the reciprocal lattice pattern forming in the expansion image, while the Mott insulator phase shows no first order coherence. (b) Demonstration that the Mott insulator transition is reversible. The lattice depth is ramped well into the Mott insulator phase and then decreased over a time $t$. For slow ramp times $t$, the superfluid phase is regained.
figures.withheld: Figure 11.15 reproduces published experimental data, which the book may not copy.

footnotes.html: The book prints $[\hat{b}_i, \hat{b}_j] = \delta_{ij}$. The bosonic operators commute to $\delta_{ij}$ with the creation operator, $[\hat{b}_i, \hat{b}_j^\dagger] = \delta_{ij}$, as the field operators do in Eq. (11.180); two annihilation operators commute, $[\hat{b}_i, \hat{b}_j] = 0$.
The book prints $\{\hat{b}_i, \hat{b}_j\} = \delta_{ij}$. The fermionic relation is $\{\hat{b}_i, \hat{b}_j^\dagger\} = \delta_{ij}$, as in Eq. (11.182), with $\{\hat{b}_i, \hat{b}_j\} = 0$.

The book calls 5.8 the exact value. It is the mean-field value $3 + 2\sqrt{2} \approx 5.83$, which the trial state of Eq. (11.211) itself reaches: its energy per site, $-z\kt|\langle\hat{b}_i\rangle|^2 + \kUzero\sin^2\ktheta/2$ with $|\langle\hat{b}_i\rangle|^2 = (1 + 1/\sqrt{2})^2\sin^2\ktheta\cos^2\ktheta$, has its least value at $\ktheta = 0$ once $\kUzero/z\kt \geq 2(1 + 1/\sqrt{2})^2$. Quantum Monte Carlo calculations for the cubic lattice give $\kUzero/z\kt \approx 4.9$ ($\kUzero/\kt \approx 29.3$; Capogrosso-Sansone, Prokof'ev and Svistunov, Phys. Rev. B 75, 134302 (2007)).

assumes.text: The overlap between wavefunctions at different sites is very small, so the interaction term is kept to leading order, $i = j = k = l$.

steps.cap: Writing $U_0 = \frac{4\pi\hbar^2a_s}{m}\int|\phi(\mathbf{r} - \mathbf{r}_i)|^4d^3\mathbf{r}$, the same on every site.

assumes.text: In one dimension the nearest neighbours of site $i$ are $i - 1$ and $i + 1$.

steps.cap: Its adjoint gives $\hat{b}_i^\dagger = \frac{1}{\sqrt{N}}\sum_k e^{-ikx_i}\hat{b}_k^\dagger$; the second sum runs over $q$.

assumes.text: The sites are spaced by $\kalat$, so $x_{i\pm1} = x_i \pm \kalat$.

nodes.note: The book prints $\cos 2\kkmag\kalat$. With neighbours $\kalat$ apart the band is $-2\kt\cos\kkmag\kalat$, of width $4\kt$.

derivations.what: the mean-field estimate of the Mott insulator to superfluid transition
derivations.source: Modern Atomic and Optical Physics II, 11.8 Cold atoms in an optical lattice, 11.8.2

assumes.text: The system is homogeneous: every site has the same energy $\kepsi$ and the same hopping $\kt_{i,j} = \kt$ to a nearest neighbor.
The state is a product of lattice-site states, so an expectation value of operators on different sites is the product of their expectation values.
$z$ is the number of nearest neighbors of a site.

steps.cap: With every $\epsilon_i$ the same, the first term is a constant energy per atom, which is dropped.
The energy per site is the expectation value of one site $i$'s terms: its interaction and its hopping to each of its $z$ neighbors $j$.
The two annihilation operators acting on the coherent state give $\alpha^2$, and the two creation operators acting to the left give $\alpha^{*2}$.

nodes.note: The book prints $\kESF = -\kt\cdot z\cdot 2 + \kUzero/2$. Each of the $z$ hopping terms of a site gives $-\kt|\kalpha|^2 = -\kt$, so the hopping energy per site is $-\kt\cdot z$, as the band of the weak lattice gives at $\kkmag = 0$: $-2\kt$ per atom for the two neighbors of one dimension.

then.why: The transition lies where the two limiting states have the same energy.

steps.cap: Where $t\cdot z \sim U_0$ and a site has several neighbors, $2t^2/U_0 \sim U_0/z^2$ is small beside $U_0/2$.

nodes.note: The book prints $\kt\cdot z\cdot 4 \sim \kUzero$, which follows from its $-\kt\cdot z\cdot 2$ in (11.208). With the hopping energy $-\kt\cdot z$ the estimate is $\kt\cdot z\cdot 2 \sim \kUzero$.
